items.excerpt: A Stanford-led team used generative AI trained on viral genomes to design 16 bacteriophages that do not exist in nature, and showed they can infect and kill drug-resistant bacteria. It is one of the first demonstrations of AI designing a whole functional genome rather than a single protein.

Chinese researchers coupled a physics-informed neural network with a GAN to correct typhoon wave-height forecasts using buoy, wind, depth and wave-energy data. The hybrid cut prediction error by up to 34.9% versus conventional numerical forecasting.

The argument: AI for science has to move past data-hungry models like AlphaFold toward reasoning agents that use tools, revise as evidence arrives, and mirror how research actually proceeds. Agents drastically reduce the need for scarce, specialized scientific datasets.

MIT's GeoPT is a pretraining method that gives simulation models a working feel for physics and geometry before task training. It generalizes to unseen scenarios like crash tests and aerodynamics while needing up to 60% less training data.

USC's Keck School built an AI assessment that fuses sweat response, brain signals and eye movements to classify depression and flag suicide risk. The goal is a biological-signal tool that helps psychiatrists identify high-risk patients earlier than self-report alone.

Harvard researchers report AI chatbot use for mental health among 12-21 year olds jumped from about 1 in 8 to nearly 1 in 5 in a single year. Most users tell neither parents nor clinicians, even though general-purpose chatbots are unvalidated for this use.

A six-question field guide for clinicians evaluating AI mental-health tools, covering legal status, evidence base and crisis-response behavior. It lands as Illinois and Nevada ban AI-delivered therapy outright while Utah and California allow it under disclosure rules.

Aalto University trained a reinforcement-learning model of human reading whose attention decisions matched real eye-tracking data, published in Nature Human Behaviour. The team says it explains rather than mimics reading, opening the door to per-reader text layout and AR displays.

South Korea's KIST developed A2SG, a training technique for spiking neural networks that reached leading ImageNet accuracy at roughly one-sixth the computational overhead of comparable methods. It targets low-power on-device AI in phones, wearables and IoT sensors.

A new quantum machine-learning framework proposes circuit architectures that mathematically avoid the exponential 'barren plateau' problem that has stalled quantum neural network training. It also cuts required circuit evaluations by roughly a factor proportional to qubit count.

items.source: EurekAlert (Wake Forest University School of Medicine)
items.excerpt: Wake Forest researchers trained an AI model that reads standard ECGs to detect three types of cardiac dysfunction, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction that routine care often misses. It held up on single-lead data of the kind wearables capture.

A Nature Medicine-anchored argument that asking whether 'AI improves healthcare' treats a dozen different technologies as one monolith. For scribes, sepsis alerts and diagnostics alike, the honest answer on patient outcomes is still often that we do not know.
